cohort: 200 late preterm and full-term infants were enrolled.
finding: Hemodynamic variables (HR, SVI, COI, and ICON) showed a significant decreasing trend over the first hour of life, and were significantly higher in vaginally delivered infants compared to those born via Cesarean section.
mod_finding: Infants delivered vaginally exhibited significantly higher heart rate, cardiac output index, stroke volume index, and index of contractility compared to those born via Cesarean section.
